chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibrahim ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves for Himself a thing and hates it for His creation. He hates for His creation the act of begging (asking from others), and loves for Himself that one should ask Him. And there is nothing more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than that one should ask Him. So let not one of you be shy to ask Allah from His Grace, even if it is just a strap of a slipper.'

key_terms.بِشِسْعِ نَعْل: A strap of a slipper (idiom for something very small/minimal)

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah love to be asked according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith distinguishes between *al-mas'ala* (begging from creatures, which is abhorrent) and *as-sual* (supplicating the Creator, which is beloved), emphasizing that divine generosity invites persistent asking. The Prophet’s closing metaphor—asking even for the 'thong of a sandal' (*shis' an-na'l*)—underscores that no need is too trivial for Allah, encouraging believers to overcome *haya'* (modesty) when addressing their Lord. This reflects the Shia theological principle that Allah’s self-sufficiency makes Him the ultimate source of all provision, rendering human dependency on Him an act of worship rather than weakness.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Dawood Bin Al Noman, from Ibrahim Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Loves something for Himself<sup>azwj</sup>, and Hates it for His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures. He<sup>azwj</sup> Hates it for His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures, the begging, and Loves for Himself<sup>azwj</sup> that one should ask Him<sup>azwj</sup>; and there is nothing more Beloved to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic than for one to ask. So not one of you should be embarrassed that he asks Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from His<sup>azwj</sup> Grace, and even though it may be a strap of a slipper’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Dawud ibn al-Nu’man from Ibrahim ibn ‘Uthman who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Allah, the Most Blessed the Most High, loves something to be for His own self and He hates something to be for His creatures. He hates His creatures begging for financial help from each other, but He loves their asking Him for help. There is nothing more beloved to Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, than being asked for help; therefore, you must not feel shy to ask Allah for favors from His generosity, even if it is as insignificant as a sandal’s strap that passes between the toes of a wearer.’”
